note: The sidebar tree. `order` is display order; `icon` names a glyph in icons.js. Nested two levels because the tree IS two levels: a department, then a garment type. MEN HAS EXACTLY ONE CHILD ON PURPOSE -- sidebar.js must render a one-child group (and a zero-child one) as a plain link, never as a disclosure, because an expand arrow that reveals a single row reads as a broken menu. Keeping a live one-child category in the skeleton is what stops that branch rotting unnoticed while the catalogue is small. A product in a category with NO subcategories carries no `sub` key at all -- data.pl requires `sub` exactly when the category has children and forbids it when it does not. There is no such category today; both have children.
